newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: At least 10 feared dead in Dutch plane crash.
newsitem.headline: At least 10 feared dead in Dutch plane crash.

text.p: A vintage propellor-driven DC-3 Dakota airliner with 35 passengers on board crashed into the North Sea on Wednesday near the Dutch naval base town of Den Helder, the coastguard said.
"Military air traffic control told us that a Dakota went down with 35 passengers on board...we are not sure how many crew the plane was carrying," a coastguard spokesman said.
The Dutch news agency ANP reported that at least 10 people had died, but the spokesman said he could not confirm the figure.
ANP reported sightings of apparently lifeless bodies still strapped into their seats, drifting in the water near the scene of the crash.
Another coastguard spokesman told Dutch radio that a number of bodies had been sighted in the water close to the crash site and that one passenger had been taken to hospital.
No details were available on the operators of the aircraft or where it was heading at the time of the crash.
Rescue vessels and helicopters had been sent to the scene, the coastguard said.
